evidence: A combines John Milton Cooper's Wilson histories with 1933 anthropology published before his 1940 birth. LC n83040704 identifies John Milton Cooper; no2003088556 identifies J. P. D. Cooper, whose York page lists both Tudor books in B. These authorities describe different people; A is already conflated.

B combines A's Victorian historian with a social-policy namesake. LC nb2001006663 identifies Hewitt (born 1962), author of Emergence of Stability and An Age of Equipoise; n92020289 identifies the welfare author (born 1945). Springer confirms the latter taught at Hertfordshire and wrote both welfare books. The authorities are distinct, but B mixes their works.

A's Helper (2003), Impending Crisis (2004), and Vagabond (2013) articles also occur in B. However, Birmingham's David Brown explicitly lists the 1999 Duke of Bedford article; B is David Christopher Brown, the American historian and Southern Outcast author. A combines two authors despite three exact matches.

LC n79077244 identifies sociologist William Isaac Thomas (1863-1947); n2014045052 identifies Rational Action author William Thomas (born 1979), distinct people. A also contains the 1995 railroad thesis associated with William G. Thomas III, whose Nebraska project biography confirms his 1995 Virginia PhD and railroad book. A is conflated and cannot merge with B.

LC n80067022 is President James Madison (1751-1836); n83209174 is Indiana historian James Henry Madison (born 1944), whose 1972 dissertation matches B. A mixes the president's writings with the historian's 1974 commercial-credit article, credited by Cambridge to James H. Madison at Indiana. The authorities are distinct, but A includes B's work.

LC n79050128 identifies James Edwin (Jim) Miller, born 1947, author of the Foucault biography and rock histories. LC n85101337 identifies James Edward Miller, born 1945, author of United States and Italy. The Italian-socialism dissertation and diplomacy books in B form a separate career from A's philosophy and music writing; these are distinct authorities, not duplicates.

LC n50006032 identifies Edward Robert Norman (born 1938), author of the Catholic Church and Ireland book; n84159513 identifies E. Herbert Norman (1909-1957). A's British and Irish church histories and B's Japan dissertation, Meiji-state history, and conscription study belong to these distinct scholars.

The 1966 Cult of True Womanhood essay was collected in Barbara Welter's Dimity Convictions (1976), directly linking A and B. Her 1978 Protestant-women missionaries article continues this research. Wisconsin's doctorate register independently confirms Barbara Welter's 1959-60 dissertation on the United States and Weimar Germany, so the earlier thesis is compatible with this career.

LC n2012018936 identifies Andrew Douglas Stewart (born 1970), the Second World War historian associated with King's College London. LC n82029531 identifies Andrew Ferguson Stewart (born 1948), author of Skopas of Paros and Greek Sculpture. A's Commonwealth military histories and B's Greek-art books belong to distinct people, not duplicate authorities.

A's initials gather multiple authors: Cambridge credits Water-Mills at Amida to Oxford archaeologist Andrew Wilson, while Irish History Online credits Constructions of Irishness to Ann Wilson. The 1925-27 Persian Gulf items add a much earlier strand. B's LC n77003675 instead identifies novelist and biographer Andrew Norman Wilson (born 1950); A cannot be assigned wholesale to him.

LC n93070452 identifies Locke historian John William Marshall (born 1961); n80067096 identifies Chief Justice John Marshall (1755-1835), distinct people. A's Locke dissertation and books fit the historian, but its 1969 Alexandria Gazette essays are the chief justice's constitutional writings, also represented in B. JSTOR confirms the essays and their McCulloch context.

LC n81004959 identifies Nigel John Harwood Smith (born 1949), author of Man, Fishes, and the Amazon. LC n94116204 identifies Nigel Scott Smith (born 1958), the Princeton literature scholar responsible for Perfection Proclaimed and Literature and Revolution. A's Amazon ecology and B's early-modern English literature belong to distinct people; the authorities are not duplicates.

LC n97119053 identifies Steven J. L. Taylor (born 1958), American University government scholar and author of Desegregation in Boston and Buffalo. LC n82132887 identifies Steven John Taylor (born 1949), the qualitative-methods author in B. Different full names, birth years, and publication careers establish distinct people despite the abbreviated label in A.

LC n83202815 identifies journalist and Librarian of Congress John Russell Young (1840-1899), whose Grant travelogue was published in 1879. LC n96103879 identifies John R. Young (born 1967), Strathclyde historian and author of The Scottish Parliament, 1639-1661. B's Scottish-history career is distinct; A's modern dates are editions of the earlier author's writings.

LC n87840594 identifies Calgary military historian John Robert Ferris (born 1956); n85078441 identifies Nottingham social-policy lecturer John Ferris (born 1937). B combines the latter's welfare and green-politics books with The British Army and Signals Intelligence, which Routledge explicitly lists as the Calgary historian's work. These authorities are distinct, but B includes A's author's book.
